classification.difficultyReason: Model the outer dimensions by adding twice the path width, subtract the field area and solve the resulting quadratic. The main decisions are representing the surrounding strip correctly and rejecting the negative width.

content.prompt: A rectangular field, 70 m long and 50 m wide, has a path of uniform width around it. If the area of the path is $1024\text{ m}^2$, find the width of the path.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the width of the path. The outside dimensions are $(70+2x)$ m and $(50+2x)$ m.

$$\begin{align*}(70+2x)(50+2x)-70\times50&=1024\\3500+240x+4x^2-3500&=1024\\4x^2+240x-1024&=0\\x^2+60x-256&=0\\(x+64)(x-4)&=0\\x+64&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-4=0\\x&=-64\quad\text{or}\quad x=4\end{align*}$$

The width is positive, so reject $x=-64$. The path is $4\text{ m}$ wide.

Check: $78\times58-70\times50=4524-3500=1024\text{ m}^2$.
